lessons: Keep narratives focused and punchy, as viewer retention drops sharply in longer or meandering formats unless tightly paced.
First-person and listener-letter narrative styles generate stronger engagement than conventional third-person radio dramas based on view patterns.
Local urban legends rooted in well-known Bengali locations (like Ultadanga or regional spots) sustain interest better than generic settings.
Structure stories with immediate atmospheric hooks within the first minute to prevent early drop-offs on YouTube.
Deliver definitive and chilling resolutions rather than ambiguous endings to satisfy horror enthusiasts in the comments.
titles: Titles featuring specific uncanny props or localized objects (like 'রক্তাক্ত কল' or specific numbers) drive significantly better click-through and watch rates.
Using dramatic imagery or visceral hooks in Title B variants successfully outperformed generic titles during A/B tests.
Keeping titles concise with a clear eerie premise works better than overly long, multi-part serial tags that confuse casual viewers.
requests: Stories involving old haunted trees that people are afraid to cut down
Interactive listener scenarios asking what the protagonist should do next (like Mohona's radio calls)
Horror elements featuring strange occurrences with household water taps or blood
Unexplained nocturnal sounds and eerie midnight noises
Encounters with mysterious strangers offering tea late at night
